text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: multiple 523/525 TLS handshake failures observed from Cloudflare edge for /v1/* endpoints starting 11:25 UTC. Error spike matching CDN pop failures and increased DNS timeouts. Severity: potential customer impact. @erica (oncall) please ACK and triage.

erica (oncall): ACK. I'm jumping on it. gathering quick scope now — are we seeing only hosted API or dedicated too?

jamie: seeing increased 5xx for hosted api keys across us-west/ca-west, some EU pops also showing handshake timeouts. Dedicated customers behind Private endpoints look OK so far.

sam: Datadog traces show TLS handshake errors with Cloudflare edge: handshake_timeout on initial SYN-ACK, and some downstream origin connectbacks failing. Also our auth provider (okta-prod) has elevated 502s for token validation around same window, might be correlated.

ophelia: Confirmed from packet captures at the border: several Cloudflare edges reporting SNI mismatch followed by abrupt FIN. Logs show `tls: handshake did not complete` in our LB for ~12% of new connections.

incident-bot: Live incident channel created: #inc-1949512345. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cloudflare-edge-failure. Start incident timeline in that channel.

erica (oncall): moving to #inc-1949512345 for live coordination. Quick impact note for customers: API requests failing with 523/525 and some 504s, retrying increases latency. CS: @raj can you surface top affected customers and if any on SLAs?

raj (cs): already getting pings from two customers in EU complaining of failed completions. Both are on hosted plan. I'll open support tickets and add incident link. Will also DM legal if any affected are enterprise with active SLAs.

sam: adding details — stack traces show `ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR` in client side, then our gateway returns 523 from Cloudflare. Observability vendor (datadog) metric ingest is also delayed — graphs sparse which is making it hard to see pop-level distribution in real time.

ophelia: I can run `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai` and `dig @1.1.1.1` — local tests show intermittent NXDOMAIN from some resolvers near west coast. Could be upstream DNS propagation or Cloudflare resolver flapping.

jamie: trying a quick mitigation: switching routing policy for critical path to bypass Cloudflare (origin direct) for the next 15m to validate impact. Will create a canary route for /v1/predict -> origin-edge-a.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: route-change/canary to LB (origin-direct) by jamie. Deploy ETA ~2m.

erica (oncall): hold on canary for 2m while we confirm token validation against Okta will still work via origin direct. Sam — will token introspection calls to okta be allowed from origin IPs? we had IP restrictions.

sam: Okta calls come from our backend; IP allowlist enforced for some enterprise orgs. For public keys validation (JWT) we don't need Okta auth calls — but if we fallback to origin-direct, our gateway will still call okta for session introspection. Need to ensure origin egress IPs are allowed. Checking now.

ophelia: I spun up a quick curl test to origin bypass for a non-enterprise key — request succeeded with normal latency. For enterprise customers with okta allowlists, we should expect failures unless we patch allowlist or use relay via bastion.

erica (oncall): decision: roll canary origin-bypass for non-enterprise traffic only. Enable rate-limited route for cookie/token signature verification path to origin-direct. Notify CS.

ram (secops-bot): Observability: Datadog reports 40% of log ingestion behind; backup logging (S3 stream) unaffected. We're pushing a partial log archive to the incident channel. Also enabling increased retention on packet captures for the next hour.

ophelia: attaching quick debug snippet:

```
# tcpdump on LB
tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp port 443' -w /tmp/cf-handshake.pcap
# sample tail of gateway log
[11:26:02] gateway: req_id=abc tls_error=handshake timeout from CF pop dfw1
[11:26:02] gateway: req_id=def client_ip=35.198.12.10 cf_edge=104.21.12.33 result=523
```

jamie: canary live. routing ~8% of traffic to origin-direct for non-enterprise. Early metrics show 60% reduction in 523s for that slice.

sam: confirm: auth provider Okta also shows elevated latencies — token introspection ~2.5s vs normal 120ms which contributes to overall tail latency when origin bypass is used.

erica (oncall): escalate to vendor ops: Cloudflare status shows partial service degradation in some POPs (link: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/abcd). Okta is reporting degraded token endpoints in EU. Datadog status mentions partial ingestion delays. We're now dealing with three dependent degradations.

ophelia: timeline note: seems correlated to a regional Cloudflare config push around 11:23 UTC — SNI routing to our edge cert may have been mis-propagated in several POPs. Packet traces show Cloudflare sending ClientHello with SNI 'api.redwood.ai' but mismatched cert selection.

jamie: mitigation plan summary:
- Maintain origin-bypass canary for non-enterprise traffic (2) 
- Route critical customers to alternate region (us-east) via traffic steering where Cloudflare POPs look healthy (3)
- Engage Cloudflare support for POP-level rollback (1) — priority escalate
- Work with Okta team to identify token endpoint issues and degrade non-essential token introspection to background for affected customers (4)

erica (oncall): I'm doing a warm handoff to @jamie in 20m for extended incident response. @sam and @ophelia continue telecom with CF/Okta.

incident-bot: Handoff scheduled: erica -> jamie at 11:45 UTC. Please update status on #inc-1949512345 for handoff notes.

sam: Cloudflare support contact acknowledged and escalated to network engineering. They've opened ticket CF-78912 and are investigating config rollback options.

ophelia: Quick customer impact blurb for status.redwood.ai: "We are investigating intermittent API errors impacting a subset of regions due to Cloudflare edge and DNS routing issues. Some customers may experience increased failures and latency. We are implementing routing mitigations. Updates ongoing."

raj (cs): posted update in customer portal and sent to affected accounts. Two enterprise customers requested immediate IP allowlist guidance for origin fallback — sending the temp IP set now.

secops-bot: Noted: there is an ongoing risk of replay attacks if we temporarily relax token introspection. Recommend keeping strict logging and short TTLs for any lifted protections.

jamie: routing more traffic to us-east and enabling origin-direct for non-enterprise reduced overall 523s by ~70%. Still seeing TLS flakey in eu-west and us-west POPs.

erica (oncall): official incident severity set to SEV2. Create postmortem ticket and assign to ophelia/sam/jamie for root cause analysis. Tagging security for any auth-related gaps.

deploy-bot: change completed: route-change/canary -> promoted to 20% traffic for non-enterprise per jamie.

ophelia: CF team reports partial rollback completed for a subset of POPs; they will continue propagation. They asked for our sample PCAPs which I uploaded.

sam: Okta has acknowledged elevated errors due to traffic spike from retry storms and are rate-throttling some endpoints. They recommend backoff and we should avoid aggressive retries in gateway for the next 10-15m.

erica (oncall): everyone, please add short notes in #inc-1949512345 on actions taken and keep timeline updates. I'll do the handoff now — jamie, take lead.

jamie: taking lead. Next steps: keep origin-bypass and region steering for another 30m, coordinate CF rollback progress, disable aggressive retry policy in gateway for 15m, monitor Datadog ingest and ensure packet captures retained for 24h. I'll post periodic updates.

raj (cs): Customers updated. No SLA breaches confirmed yet but I'm preparing export of error traces for legal/AM review just in case.

secops-bot: Reminder: collect keys and token logs for any enterprise accounts that experienced fallback to origin-direct for audit.

jamie: closing live coordination for now — will post a summary at 12:15 UTC or earlier if material changes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident note: next update scheduled at 12:15 UTC. Incident channel archived to be used for postmortem notes after resolution.
